input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per-year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights." That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback, which permits at most a commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a penalty. It also conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and with the termination rights in Section 9. We propose the preferred position: no minimum commitment, payment only for Services used or ordered (consistent with Section 7.1's fees-per-Order-Form construct), with a 12-month reducible commitment plus true-up available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Remove three-year take-or-pay minimum commitment; pay only for Services used or ordered
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment because our playbook does not accept minimum purchase commitments without a reduction or exit right, and it contradicts Section 12.3's confirmation that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If a commitment is commercially essential, we could consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.

ops.newText: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase commitment. Customer will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term.
